# Register reference {#registers}

This appendix lists the registers of LiteSATA: PHY, Identify, BIST, DMAs and interrupts.
It is generated from the register definitions of the gateware, elaborated on the
control/DMA example `examples/ultrascale_plus_axi_lite_dma.yml` of the generator,
without running an FPGA toolchain. Offsets are in
bytes from the base of the bank; the base addresses depend on the SoC and are in the
`csr.csv` of a build. A LiteX SoC names the banks after the `name` given to `add_sata`,
`sata` by default, as in this example.

| Configuration | Target and options |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `usp_axi_lite_dma` | `litesata_gen` `ultrascale_plus_axi_lite_dma.yml` |

Access is `rw` for a register written by software (`CSRStorage`, or a `CSRStatus` that
software also writes, such as event pending bits cleared by writing 1), `ro` for a status
(`CSRStatus`) and `wo` for a write-only strobe (`CSR`). The reset value of a `CSRStorage`
register ends its description. A register wider than 32 bits takes several
32-bit words of the bus, most significant word first. The BIOS, `liblitesata` and the host scripts of
`bench/` use these names through the generated `csr.h` and `csr.csv`, so they rarely need the offsets.

## PHY {#reg-sata-phy}

Defined by `LiteSATAPHY` (`litesata/phy/__init__.py`).

Present when the PHY is built with `with_csr=True`, the default. The bank is the same
for every transceiver family, ECP5 included. The BIOS `sata_init` and
`bench/test_init.py` toggle `enable` to restart the link, then poll `status` until
`ready` is set ([PHY architecture and OOB controller](#phy-architecture)).

Bank `sata_phy`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `enable` | `0x0000` | 1 | rw | PHY enable: 0 holds the transceiver initialization in reset, 1 lets it run and the OOB sequence start. Reset `0x1`. |
| `status` | `0x0004` | 5 | ro | PHY status. |

Fields of `status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `ready` | 0 | 1: transceiver and controller ready, the link carries the core traffic. |
| `tx_ready` | 1 | 1: transceiver TX initialized. |
| `rx_ready` | 2 | 1: transceiver RX initialized. |
| `ctrl_ready` | 3 | 1: OOB and ALIGN handshake of the PHY controller complete. |
| `link_up` | 4 | 1: link up, debounced: falls after `link_down_timeout` (100 ms) without `ready`. |

## Identify {#reg-sata-identify}

Defined by `LiteSATAIdentifyCSR` (`litesata/frontend/identify.py`).

Present with `with_identify` of `add_sata`, default on. Software writes `start`, waits
for `done`, then reads the 128 dwords (256 words) of the IDENTIFY data: it reads
`source_data` while `source_valid` is set and writes `source_ready` after each dword
([Frontends](#frontends)).

Bank `sata_identify`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `start` | `0x0000` | 1 | wo | Write 1: empty the data FIFO and send an IDENTIFY DEVICE command. |
| `done` | `0x0004` | 1 | ro | 1: idle, no command in progress. |
| `data_width` | `0x0008` | 16 | ro | Width of the user port, in bits. |
| `source_valid` | `0x000c` | 1 | ro | 1: a dword of the IDENTIFY data is in `source_data`. |
| `source_ready` | `0x0010` | 1 | wo | Write 1: pop the dword of `source_data`. |
| `source_data` | `0x0014` | 32 | ro | Current dword of the IDENTIFY data (FIFO of 512 dwords, 128 used). |
| `error` | `0x0018` | 1 | ro | 1: the last command failed (drive error or CRC error). |

## BIST generator {#reg-sata-bist-generator}

Defined by `LiteSATABISTUnitCSR` (`litesata/frontend/bist.py`).

Present with `with_bist` of `add_sata`, or with `LiteSATABIST(with_csr=True)` in the
bench targets. The generator writes `count` sectors from `sector`, `loops` times. The
throughput of a run is `loops*count*512/(cycles/clk_freq)` bytes per second, the
formula of `bench/test_bist.py`. The `errors` register of the generator stays at 0.

The generator, the checker and the Identify unit of the BIST share the `sata_bist`
bank: their full names start with `sata_bist_generator_`, `sata_bist_checker_` and
`sata_bist_identify_`, and their offsets are from the base of `sata_bist`.

Bank `sata_bist_generator`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `start` | `0x0000` | 1 | wo | Write 1: run `loops` commands on `count` sectors from `sector`. |
| `sector` | `0x0004` | 48 | rw | First sector (48-bit LBA). Reset `0x0`. |
| `count` | `0x000c` | 16 | rw | Number of sectors per command. Reset `0x0`. |
| `loops` | `0x0010` | 8 | rw | Number of commands of a run. Reset `0x0`. |
| `random` | `0x0014` | 1 | rw | Data pattern: 0 counter, 1 scrambler (pseudo-random). Reset `0x0`. |
| `done` | `0x0018` | 1 | ro | 1: idle, run finished or never started. |
| `aborted` | `0x001c` | 1 | ro | 1: the last command of the run failed (drive error or CRC error). |
| `errors` | `0x0020` | 32 | ro | Dwords read back with a wrong value in the last command (checker only). |
| `cycles` | `0x0024` | 32 | ro | System clock cycles of the whole run. |

## BIST checker {#reg-sata-bist-checker}

Defined by `LiteSATABISTUnitCSR` (`litesata/frontend/bist.py`).

Same layout as the generator. The checker reads the sectors back and counts the dwords
that differ from the pattern the generator writes with the same `sector` and `random`.
Each command of a run clears `errors` and `aborted`, so they report the last command.

Bank `sata_bist_checker`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `start` | `0x0028` | 1 | wo | Write 1: run `loops` commands on `count` sectors from `sector`. |
| `sector` | `0x002c` | 48 | rw | First sector (48-bit LBA). Reset `0x0`. |
| `count` | `0x0034` | 16 | rw | Number of sectors per command. Reset `0x0`. |
| `loops` | `0x0038` | 8 | rw | Number of commands of a run. Reset `0x0`. |
| `random` | `0x003c` | 1 | rw | Data pattern: 0 counter, 1 scrambler (pseudo-random). Reset `0x0`. |
| `done` | `0x0040` | 1 | ro | 1: idle, run finished or never started. |
| `aborted` | `0x0044` | 1 | ro | 1: the last command of the run failed (drive error or CRC error). |
| `errors` | `0x0048` | 32 | ro | Dwords read back with a wrong value in the last command (checker only). |
| `cycles` | `0x004c` | 32 | ro | System clock cycles of the whole run. |

## BIST Identify {#reg-sata-bist-identify}

Defined by `LiteSATAIdentifyCSR` (`litesata/frontend/bist.py`).

The BIST has its own Identify unit, with the layout of the Identify bank, so that a
bench target needs no other frontend to read the drive information.

Bank `sata_bist_identify`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `start` | `0x0050` | 1 | wo | Write 1: empty the data FIFO and send an IDENTIFY DEVICE command. |
| `done` | `0x0054` | 1 | ro | 1: idle, no command in progress. |
| `data_width` | `0x0058` | 16 | ro | Width of the user port, in bits. |
| `source_valid` | `0x005c` | 1 | ro | 1: a dword of the IDENTIFY data is in `source_data`. |
| `source_ready` | `0x0060` | 1 | wo | Write 1: pop the dword of `source_data`. |
| `source_data` | `0x0064` | 32 | ro | Current dword of the IDENTIFY data (FIFO of 512 dwords, 128 used). |
| `error` | `0x0068` | 1 | ro | 1: the last command failed (drive error or CRC error). |

## Sector2Mem DMA {#reg-sata-sector2mem}

Defined by `LiteSATASector2MemDMA` (`litesata/frontend/dma.py`).

Present when the `mode` of `add_sata` contains `read`. The DMA reads `nsectors`
sectors from `sector` and writes them to memory from `base`, 512 bytes per sector,
with one READ DMA EXT command per sector. The end test compares the current sector
with `sector + nsectors - 1`, so a transfer with `nsectors` at 0 does not end.

Bank `sata_sector2mem`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `sector` | `0x0000` | 48 | rw | First sector (48-bit LBA). Reset `0x0`. |
| `nsectors` | `0x0008` | 16 | rw | Number of sectors, one ATA command per sector; must not be 0. Reset `0x0`. |
| `base` | `0x000c` | 64 | rw | Byte address of the memory buffer. Reset `0x0`. |
| `start` | `0x0014` | 1 | wo | Write: start the transfer. |
| `done` | `0x0018` | 1 | ro | 1: idle, transfer finished or never started. |
| `error` | `0x001c` | 1 | ro | 1: a command of the transfer failed; the transfer stopped there. |

## Mem2Sector DMA {#reg-sata-mem2sector}

Defined by `LiteSATAMem2SectorDMA` (`litesata/frontend/dma.py`).

Present when the `mode` of `add_sata` contains `write`. It mirrors Sector2Mem: one
WRITE DMA EXT command per sector, with the same rule on `nsectors`.

Bank `sata_mem2sector`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `sector` | `0x0000` | 48 | rw | First sector (48-bit LBA). Reset `0x0`. |
| `nsectors` | `0x0008` | 16 | rw | Number of sectors, one ATA command per sector; must not be 0. Reset `0x0`. |
| `base` | `0x000c` | 64 | rw | Byte address of the memory buffer. Reset `0x0`. |
| `start` | `0x0014` | 1 | wo | Write: start the transfer. |
| `done` | `0x0018` | 1 | ro | 1: idle, transfer finished or never started. |
| `error` | `0x001c` | 1 | ro | 1: a command of the transfer failed; the transfer stopped there. |

## Interrupts {#reg-sata-irq}

Defined by the `add_sata` method of the LiteX SoC (`soc.py` of LiteX).

Present with `with_irq` of `add_sata`, default on: a LiteX event manager with one pulse
event per DMA, raised when the DMA terminates, after its last sector or on an error.
Writing 1 to a bit of `pending` clears it. The link events of the PHY (`connect_irq`,
`disconnect_irq`) are not wired to it.

Bank `sata_irq`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `status` | `0x0000` | 2 | ro | This register contains the current raw level of the event trigger. Writes to this register have no effect. |
| `pending` | `0x0004` | 2 | rw | When an event occurs, the corresponding bit will be set in this register. To clear the Event, set the corresponding bit in this register. |
| `enable` | `0x0008` | 2 | rw | This register enables the corresponding events. Write a ``0`` to this register to disable individual events. Reset `0x0`. |

Fields of `status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `sector2mem_dma` | 0 | Level of the ``sector2mem_dma`` event. |
| `mem2sector_dma` | 1 | Level of the ``mem2sector_dma`` event. |

Fields of `pending`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `sector2mem_dma` | 0 | Sector2Mem DMA terminated. |
| `mem2sector_dma` | 1 | Mem2Sector DMA terminated. |

Fields of `enable`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `sector2mem_dma` | 0 | Write a ``1`` to enable the ``sector2mem_dma`` Event. |
| `mem2sector_dma` | 1 | Write a ``1`` to enable the ``mem2sector_dma`` Event. |
